answer: Cross-cluster quorum admission requires a newcomer to post a crystal onto the routing meadow only after collecting signatures from pairwise-disjoint trust branches. The meadow traces the candidate's settlement graph and groups accounts sharing funding paths onto the same ledge. Registering the $m$-th identity on a ledge requires $3m$ distinct branch signatures, each locking 10 ETH of the signer's stake into that crystal. A solo newcomer needs 3 signatures locking 30 ETH, whereas an operator adding $n$ sybils on one ledge must bribe $3n(n+1)/2$ independent branches to lock $15n(n+1)$ ETH.
